t.6.62.1: Then the greatly splendorous Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, spoke, making his request known to the wise and mighty Hanumān.
t.6.62.3: Whichever monkeys there are who are mighty and swift, let those bulls among the monkeys seize firebrands and quickly leap up against Laṅkā.
t.6.62.2: Since Kumbhakarṇa has been slain and the princes have been killed, Rāvaṇa is now in no position to mount a counterattack.
t.6.62.4: Then, when the sun had gone to its setting, at that dreadful onset of night, those bulls among the monkeys, bearing firebrands, went forth facing Laṅkā.
t.6.62.5: Assailed from every side by hosts of monkeys bearing firebrands in their hands, the ugly-eyed guards stationed at their posts suddenly fled in all directions.
t.6.62.6: Thrilled with excitement, they set fire to the gate-towers, the watchtowers and the streets, to the various thoroughfares, and to the palaces.
t.6.62.7: Then the fire, the devourer of oblations, burned thousands of their houses, and the dwellings of all the rākṣasas who were householders.
t.6.62.8: Of those whose armour was bright with gold, who wore garlands, wreaths and fine garments, whose eyes rolled from drinking sīdhu, and whose gait was unsteady with intoxication.
t.6.62.9: Of those whose garments were held by their beloved women, in whom fury against the enemy had arisen, who bore maces, spears and swords in their hands, and who went on eating and drinking as well.
t.6.62.10: Of those who had been sleeping with their beloved ones on costly beds, and who, terrified, were fleeing swiftly in every direction, taking their sons with them…
t.6.62.11: Then the fire burned thousands of houses of those dwellers of Laṅkā, and there it blazed up again and again.
t.6.62.12: They were solid and costly, endowed with profound excellences, adorned with golden moons and half-moons, and rising lofty with their rooftop pavilions.
t.6.62.13: Everywhere they stood on firm foundations, their windows bright with jewels, adorned with gems and coral, and they seemed almost to touch the sun.
t.6.62.14: That fire burned down the mansions, lofty as mountains, which had echoed with the cries of krauñca birds and peacocks, the strains of vīṇās, and the jingling of ornaments.
t.6.62.15: Surrounded by fire, the gateways shone like masses of clouds laced with lightning at the close of the hot season.
t.6.62.16: And the beautiful women who had been sleeping in the palaces, being burned, cast off their ornaments and cried out loudly, "Alas! Alas!"
t.6.62.17: And there the mansions too, engulfed by fire, came crashing down, like the peaks of a great mountain struck by the thunderbolt of the Thunderbolt-wielder.
t.6.62.18: Being consumed by fire, they shone brightly from afar, like the peaks of Himavat and like forests of glowing herbs.
t.6.62.19: With the tops of its mansions burning and blazing with flames, Laṅkā appeared at night as though covered with flowering kiṃśuka trees.
t.6.62.20: With the elephant-keepers, with the elephants let loose and the horses set free as well, Laṅkā became like the ocean at the end of the world, its crocodiles roaming wildly about.
t.6.62.22: In a moment that city, set ablaze by the monkeys, became like the earth burning at the terrible destruction of this world.
t.6.62.21: Seeing a horse running loose, an elephant, frightened, draws back a little; and here and there a horse, itself afraid, turns back on seeing a frightened elephant.
t.6.62.23: The cry of the womenfolk, enveloped in smoke, scorched by the blazing fire and wailing loudly, was heard for ten yojanas.
t.6.62.24: Then the monkeys, eager for battle, suddenly sprang upon the other rākṣasas who had come outside with their bodies badly burned.
t.6.62.25: The roaring of the monkeys and the clamor of the rākṣasas made the ten directions, the ocean and the earth resound.
t.6.62.26: Then the two great-souled ones, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, both freed from the arrows, calmly and without agitation took up their two excellent bows.
t.6.62.27: Then, as Rāma stretched his excellent bow, there arose a tumultuous sound that brought terror to the rākṣasas.
t.6.62.28: Then Rāma, stretching his mighty bow, shone forth like the blessed Bhava, enraged, stretching his bow made of the Vedas.
t.6.62.29: The tumult raised by the shouting vānaras, the clamor of the rākṣasas, and the twang of Rāma's bowstring as well, these three together pervaded the ten directions.
t.6.62.30: And struck by the arrows loosed from his bow, that city-gate tower, resembling a peak of Kailāsa, fell shattered upon the ground.
t.6.62.31: Then, seeing Rāma's arrows on the palaces and in the houses, the lords of the rākṣasas fell to arming themselves in tumultuous haste.
t.6.62.32: As those lords of the Rākṣasas armed themselves for battle and raised their lion-like roars, the night became as if terrible.
t.6.62.33: Those lords of the monkeys were commanded by the great-souled Sugrīva: "Draw near, reach the gate, and fight, O bulls among the leaping monkeys!"
t.6.62.34: And whoever among you, stationed here and there, should act falsely, that violator of the king's command must be rushed upon and slain.
t.6.62.35: When those foremost of the monkeys, their hands bright with blazing firebrands, had reached the gate and stood there, rage took possession of Rāvaṇa.
t.6.62.36: By the convulsion of his yawning the ten directions were thrown into confusion, and in his limbs the wrath of Rudra was seen, as though it had taken bodily form.
t.6.62.37: Enraged, he dispatched both Nikumbha and Kumbha, the two sons of Kumbhakarṇa, together with many rākṣasas.
t.6.62.38: And the lord of the rākṣasas commanded all those rākṣasas, sounding a lion's roar: "Rākṣasas, go right here!"
t.6.62.39: Then, urged on by him, the heroic Rākṣasas, their weapons blazing, sallied forth from Laṅkā, roaring again and again.
t.6.62.40: It was an army of fearsome horses, chariots and elephants, thronged with foot soldiers of many kinds, and bristling with blazing spears, maces, swords, lances, javelins and bows.
t.6.62.41: That terrible army of rākṣasas, of fearsome valour and manly might, was seen with its blazing lances, resounding with hundreds of tinkling bells.
t.6.62.42: Him, whose arms were adorned with networks of gold, whose battle-axe was bound fast about him, who whirled a mighty weapon, and whose bow was fitted with arrows.
t.6.62.44: Seeing that most dreadful army of the rākṣasas advancing, the army of the monkeys was shaken and roared aloud.
t.6.62.43: It was a place whose mighty wind was made fragrant by the outpouring of perfumes, garlands and honeyed wine; terrible, thronged with heroic men, and resounding with a roar like that of great rain-clouds.
t.6.62.45: Leaping swiftly once more over that great army of rākṣasas, he rushed against the opposing host as a moth rushes into a fire.
t.6.62.46: The excellent army of those rākṣasas, its iron clubs and thunderbolt-weapons burnished by the grasp of their arms, shone forth all the more brilliantly.
t.6.62.47: Likewise, other night-roaming rākṣasas of dreadful form struck down on all sides the foremost heroes among those monkeys with their sharpened swords.
t.6.62.48: One struck down another who was striking, another felled one who was felling; one reviled another who was reviling, and yet another bit one who was biting.
t.6.62.49: "Give!" cried one, while another gave, and yet another said, "I am giving!" "Why do you trouble me? Stop!" So they spoke to one another there.
t.6.62.50: There ensued a most terrible battle between the monkeys and the rākṣasas, in which great lances were raised aloft and which was thronged with fists, spears and swords.
t.6.62.51: The rākṣasas struck down the vānaras by tens and by sevens, and in the battle the vānaras slew the rākṣasas by tens and by sevens.
t.6.62.52: Seizing upon the rākṣasa army, its hair and girdles loosened, its armor and banners cast off, the monkeys surrounded it on all sides.
